extra.message: Sensitive internal endpoints protected only by a single static shared-secret header — A single leaked static token grants unauthenticated remote attackers access to RCE, arbitrary file write, XXE, and PII-dumping endpoints [verified: _wrk_gate is a single static env-var secret compared with '==' (not constant-time) and no rate limiting, gating access to RCE/XXE/file-write endpoints — a genuinely weak authentication control.]

Server-side template injection via GET fragment — Remote code execution / full server compromise via Jinja2 SSTI-to-RCE gadget chains [verified: fragment is concatenated into Jinja2 template source and rendered, enabling SSTI-to-RCE; no sanitization present.]

OS command injection via unsanitized host parameter — Remote code execution on the application server as the app's OS user [verified: Unsanitized host is concatenated into os.system with no escaping; _wrk_gate is only a static shared-secret header, not real authz, so this is exploitable RCE.]

Hardcoded insecure default SECRET_KEY fallback — Attacker who knows/guesses the fallback key can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, or signed URLs, leading to authentication bypass [verified: Line 19 hardcodes a known fallback SECRET_KEY string used whenever DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is absent, enabling session/CSRF forgery in any deployment missing that env var.]

Insecure-by-default DEBUG and SECRET_KEY fallbacks — Verbose debug pages leaking source code and settings; forgeable sessions/CSRF tokens if the default secret key reaches production [verified: Line 20 defaults DEBUG to True and line 19 falls back to a hardcoded SECRET_KEY when env vars are unset; no override elsewhere in settings.py.]

DEBUG defaults to True in production settings — Verbose Django debug pages leak source code, settings (SECRET_KEY, DB creds), and request data to any user who triggers an unhandled exception [verified: Confirmed identical to idx 0: DEBUG defaults True on line 20 with no other DEBUG assignment in the file, exposing debug pages/tracebacks by default.]

Mass assignment of privileged fields (is_admin, credit_limit) from client JSON — Privilege escalation / business-logic bypass by directly setting protected fields [verified: change_set parsed from raw client JSON is merged via dict.update into a dict containing is_admin/credit_limit with no allowlist, letting a caller override those fields.]

Sensitive credential and PII exposure in API response — Disclosure of a partner integration token and PII (SSN-like value) to any caller possessing the shared ops header, enabling downstream partner-API abuse or identity theft [verified: Hardcoded partner sync token and SSN-shaped tax_ref are returned to any caller passing the shared header, with no per-tenant scoping.]

Path traversal leading to arbitrary file write — Arbitrary file write on the server, potentially leading to code execution via overwritten application files [verified: ref is inserted directly into a filesystem path under BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no traversal sanitization before write_text.]

Plaintext storage/exposure of PII (SSN, card number) and live-looking tokens — Disclosure of sensitive PII and an apparent live partner sync token, persisted unencrypted or returned in responses [verified: course_vault_stash_245 writes ssn/card values to plaintext JSON on disk and course_roster_fold_066 returns a hardcoded SSN-shaped tax_ref and live-looking sync_key in the response body.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses from this endpoint [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, permitting any origin credentialed cross-origin reads.]

Path traversal in arbitrary file write endpoint — Arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory, potentially overwriting application files or planting files in served static/media paths for further compromise [verified: name is joined directly under BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no '..' sanitization and raw request body is written to that path via write_bytes, enabling arbitrary file write.]

XXE via unsafe lxml parser configuration — Arbitrary local file read, SSRF to internal/network resources via external entities [verified: XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False on attacker-controlled request.body enables classic XXE.]

Missing Secure flag on session/CSRF cookies — Session/CSRF cookies transmitted over unencrypted HTTP can be intercepted by a network-position attacker, enabling session hijacking [verified: settings.py sets SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY/CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY but never sets SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, or SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, so cookies are sent over plain HTTP by default.]

Reflected XSS via copyline parameter — Reflected cross-site scripting; session/token theft or actions on behalf of a victim who reaches the endpoint [verified: copyline is concatenated unescaped into an HTML response returned as text/html, a classic reflected XSS sink.]

Missing authentication check on ops endpoint — Unauthenticated access to an internal ops endpoint [verified: course_identity_ping_341 indeed omits the _wrk_gate check present on all sibling handlers, making it reachable without any token.]

Account enumeration and brute-forceable verifier with no rate limiting — Attacker can enumerate valid handles from the error codes, then brute-force the low-entropy 4-digit verifier to gain elevated 'lane' status without any throttling [verified: Distinct 404 vs 403 responses directly disclose valid handles, and the 4-digit verifier is checked with no rate limiting or lockout, enabling enumeration plus brute force.]

Weak PRNG used to generate security-relevant codes — Generated codes are predictable given enough samples of the PRNG state, allowing an attacker to guess or reproduce codes intended to be secret/unguessable [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) generates a supposedly secret code with attacker-controlled length instead of secrets/os.urandom.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle interception or tampering of outbound partner communications [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used for the outbound urlopen call, disabling certificate validation on partner communication.]

Weak cryptographic hash (MD5) used for digest generation — MD5 digests can be brute-forced or reversed via rainbow tables, undermining any integrity/verification guarantee the endpoint is meant to provide [verified: MD5 is used to produce a 'digest' with no salt or modern algorithm; while this specific endpoint's use is low-impact, it is a real weak-crypto instance as reported.]

CSV formula/DDE injection in grade & submission exports via attacker-controlled username — Client-side code execution / data exfiltration against the school admin who opens the exported CSV, triggered purely via self-registration through a normal invitation link [verified: Username is fully attacker-chosen via self-service invitation acceptance and flows unsanitized into CSV export via DictWriter with no leading-character escaping, matching classic CSV formula injection; impact is limited to client-side execution in the admin's spreadsheet app upon opening.]
